correctness.rationale: The torus weights make both monomials x^2y and z^3w^2 product_i u_i^2 invariant. On x != 0, normalization x=1 identifies the quotient with A^(n+2), and this covers the complement of the divisor x=0. On x=0 the equation forces u_1 != 0, so the u_1 chart has coordinates q=xu_1,b=y/u_1^2,c=zu_1^2,d=w/u_1^2,U_i=u_i (i>=2) satisfying q^2 b+c^3d^2 product U_i^2=1. The divisor q=0 is parametrized globally by b, s=(c d product U_i)^(-1) and U_2..U_n, with c=s^2 and d=s^(-3) product U_i^(-1), proving D ≅ A^1 x (C*)^n and a trivial normal line defined by invariant q in a whole neighborhood. Both chart normalizations also establish trivial stabilizers. The homotopy-pushout Y=U union N(D), U contractible, identifies Y with Thom of that normal line; triviality gives Sigma^2 (D_+) ≃ wedge_r binom(n,r) S^(r+2). This yields all integral cohomology, vanishing positive cup products and pi_1=0. I independently verified the monomial weights, q/c/d coordinate identities and binomial ranks for small n; the all-n result uses standard tubular neighborhoods and suspension splitting, not numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: The homotopy type and torsion-free integral cohomology of a geometrically motivated family of smooth generically flexible but non-flexible affine quotients are natural topological invariants that can aid comparison and obstruction arguments. The two-chart description yields an entire all-n wedge-of-spheres classification, not merely low-degree Betti numbers or generic smoothness; this is a meaningful structural refinement of the original algebraic construction.

limitations: An unindexed algebraic topological calculation of exactly this quotient could exist.
The wedge splitting is classical *complex* homotopy only; no algebraic A1-homotopy statement is justified.
The topological pushout needs correct tubular-neighborhood cofibration setup, addressed by smooth closed D and contractible open complement.
